name: Sirāj al-Dīn Abū Yaʿqūb Yūsuf ibn Abī Bakr al-Sakkākī
summary: Khwārazmian scholar whose Miftāḥ al-ʿulūm joins ṣarf, naḥw and rhetoric in one book; its third part became, through al-Qazwīnī's abridgement, the rhetoric of the madrasa.
bio: Al-Sakkākī was born in Khwārazm in 555/1160. His name means 'the smith', and the biographers tell that he worked metal until he was thirty, made a fine piece for the ruler, saw the ruler turn from it to honour a scholar who came in, and set himself to study; the story is told to show that it is never too late.

His Miftāḥ al-ʿulūm, 'the key of the sciences', is in three parts: ṣarf with derivation, naḥw, and the sciences of meaning and expression (maʿānī and bayān), with sections on definition, argument and the metres. The third part, abridged by al-Qazwīnī in Talkhīṣ al-Miftāḥ and explained by al-Taftāzānī, is what the madrasas read as balāgha; the first two parts were read less but show the same ordering mind. He died in 626/1229.

sources.title: Sekkâkî, Ebû Ya'kūb, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
